text:
jamie: Customer (Acme Corp) reporting intermittent 502 + TLS handshake errors when calling our private inference endpoint from their VPC. Started ~0900 UTC, ~10% of requests high latency then fail.

sara: Any error logs from our side or customer side? Is this Dedicated or Private (VPC) deployment?

jamie: Private VPC deployment. Customer sent a short repro: curl from an instance in their private subnet -> our endpoint returns TLS error. From their bastion (public) same curl succeeds.

mike: Can you paste the curl output and any server-side logs? Also, what path/port are they hitting (443 or custom)?

jamie: They hit standard 443. Here's curl from their app host (inside private subnet):

```
$ curl -v https://redwood-infer-prd.acme.internal/predict
* Rebuilt URL to: https://redwood-infer-prd.acme.internal/predict
*   Trying 10.200.3.12...
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connected to redwood-infer-prd.acme.internal (10.200.3.12) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.2 connection attempt, handshake failed
* SSL: error:1408A0C1:SSL routines:ssl3_get_client_hello:no shared cipher
* Closing connection 0
curl: (35) SSL: error:1408A0C1:SSL routines:ssl3_get_client_hello:no shared cipher
```

jamie: Server logs show repeated TLS handshake timeouts and then 502s for those requests.

infra-bot: Incident INC-9012 created (priority: p2) — Assigned to #support.

mike: That cipher error can be a red herring if the TCP/TLS flow is being reset or middlebox-modified. Can we get a tcpdump from the app host for a failing request? Prefer capture of SYN..TLS ClientHello.

jamie: Customer provided a short tcpdump snippet. Key bits below (timestamps removed for brevity):

```
1. 10.1.5.21 > 10.200.3.12: TCP 52344 -> 443 SYN
2. 10.200.3.12 > 10.1.5.21: TCP 443 -> 52344 RST
3. repeated SYNs, then connection reset
```

mike: RST from 10.200.3.12 is odd — could be NAT/NGW or firewall sending RST when it has no state. Which infra component owns 10.200.3.12? Is that the customer NAT or our NLB?

jamie: 10.200.3.12 is their NAT gateway IP (customer-provided). Our endpoint IPs are in a different range; the dump is captured from their side after NAT translation. Customer also supplied NACL and SG configs.

sara: Paste their NACL/SG rules. Look for explicit DENY ranges, especially ephemeral ports (1024-65535) or asymmetric rules on return traffic. Stateful SGs vs stateless NACL mix often causes this.

jamie: NACL (inbound to their private subnet):
- Rule 100: ALLOW TCP 443 from 0.0.0.0/0
- Rule 110: DENY ALL 1024-65535 from 0.0.0.0/0
(They have explicit deny for high ports. SG outbound allows 443 only.)

mike: There it is — NACL is stateless. When our server responds from a high source port (>1024) during the TLS handshake or for keepalive flows, the NACL inbound rule denies those return packets. The NAT gateway translates ports, so the return traffic will hit ephemeral port ranges on the customer side and be dropped. That explains TCP RST/handshake failures.

ops: Confirmed pattern: initial TCP three-way sometimes completes then server tries to open a new client-initiated connection or send a FIN from high port and gets dropped. Also impacts TLS session resumption / keepalive which can use ephemeral ports for backend->client flows in some topologies.

sara: Action items for customer: allow ephemeral ranges or remove the DENY rule. We should give exact rule guidance.

mike: Suggested NACL config (customer-side) — minimal change:
- Edit inbound rules on the private-subnet NACL to allow TCP ephemeral ephemeral ports: 1024-65535 from 0.0.0.0/0
- Or remove the explicit DENY 1024-65535 entry so return packets from our services are accepted.

sara: Also confirm Security Group outbound can reach 443 and ephemeral for responses (SGs are stateful so outbound 443 is fine but NACL is the blocker). Example SG outbound rule (already present):
- Type: HTTPS | Protocol: TCP | Port range: 443 | Destination: 0.0.0.0/0

jamie: I drafted a short troubleshooting checklist to send to customer: 
1) Temporarily remove the NACL DENY 1024-65535 and retest.
2) If they require restrictive NACLs, add explicit ALLOW inbound 1024-65535 from our CIDR(s) (we provided our egress CIDRs in earlier onboarding).
3) Confirm NAT gateway healthcheck ICMP not blocked (some stateful flows depend on ICMP unreachable for PMTU).
4) Run `curl --resolve redwood-infer-prd.acme.internal:<endpoint-ip>:443 -v` from app host and capture tcpdump during the test.

mike: Also include note about asymmetric routing: if they have multiple NATs, ensure return path goes through the same NAT (stateful mapping) or allow ephemeral ranges on all NACLs.

ops: Customer applied ALLOW for 1024-65535 inbound on NACL and reported immediate improvement. No more TLS handshake errors after ~10 minutes of drift.

jamie: Customer confirms service stable, no more 502s. They left this note: "Thanks — we had a hardened NACL template that denies high ports; toggling that off fixed it. We'll add our provider CIDRs to the allowlist." :tada:

sara: Please add a KB blurb for private deployment onboarding: note to avoid DENY on ephemeral ranges in NACLs and list common symptoms (TLS handshake errors, RSTs in tcpdump, intermittent 502s).

mike: I'll file KB draft and attach example diagrams and iptables/nacl rule snippets.

jamie: Closing INC-9012 after customer validation. infra-bot: close INC-9012.

infra-bot: Incident INC-9012 marked resolved (resolved_by: jamie).
